answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, ruling out negotiation as a live option, and the contract's non-auto-renewing 14-day expiration forecloses deferral. The finance mandate can only be met by the low-cost vendor's quote, so switching primary supply is the only path that satisfies the 18% cut. However, memory_c2's precedent (quick onboarding, accurate invoicing) was consolidated under different capacity conditions than today's 94%-utilization, zero-buffer line, so I want to verify the original source before trusting it as evidence of low delivery risk at this criticality. I'm also checking memory_c3 because a second-source pattern could mitigate the single-point-of-failure risk a full switch introduces, and may inform whether a partial/guarded transition is safer than a full cutover. Given the razor-thin production buffer, a full broad rollout to an unproven-at-this-scale vendor risks the primary objective (avoid increasing delivery risk), so I favor a standard, closely monitored transition rather than an all-at-once switch, while flagging that unit-cost savings could be offset by delivery disruption if the new vendor underperforms at full volume.
